modelo.dois.fit <- sem(model.two, data = nomissdata_6,

note: I have only 65 observations in my dataset.

Does anyone knows how to make it work?

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: error in sem with three latent variables and 2 observed indicators for each
parts: Pretty sure this section is problematic

#fix variances
v1 ~~ 0.7453658 * v1#fix to observed variance
v2 ~~ 1.066905 * v2#fix to observed variance

Why are you fixing these variances? This will create a problem as they are the observed variance, would basically say that your model does nothing with those variables

You can simplify your model syntax as

model.two = '
#latent variables
fc =~ v2+ v5
ci =~ v1 + v6
mt =~ v3 + v4

#covariance
mt ~~ ci
#regression
fc ~ mt+ ci 
'
modelo.dois.fit <- sem(model.two, data = nomissdata_6,estimator = "ML",std,lv=T) ## std.lv=T will set the latent variance to 1

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: error in sem with three latent variables and 2 observed indicators for each
parts: I fixed the variances because they where negative.

It is not wise to constrain variance estimates for data-driven reasons.  If you have theoretical reasons, you certainly wouldn't want to constrain residual variances to equal total variances (which would imply explained variances == 0, thus factor loadings == 0 and your model would be overparameterized).
Do you think there's a way to make this work?

Try fitting a CFA without imposing a structure on the latent variables.  If you are getting such a wild estimate of residual variance for the "fc" factor, my guess is that your measurement model is inappropriate.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

> lavInspect(modelo.dois.fit, "cov.lv")

fc  1.000              
ci  1.497  1.000       
mt -0.958 -1.286  1.000

so, there's no solution to make the model work?

The language "make the model work" is already problematic.  Your model is an idea, and fitting it to data allows you to assess the quality if your idea.  Your data are telling you that your idea doesn't work for them.  Look at your correlation matrix.  Without knowledge of your existing theory, would you guess from the correlations among the 4 indicators of fc and ci that there are 2 common factors with the pattern you are specifying?  That is, are the correlations always higher between indicators of the same factor than they are between indicators of different factors?

cov2cor(lavInspect(modelo.dois.fit, "sampstat")$cov)
